outcome: efficacy of sutures (controlling hemorrhage, avoiding hysterectomy)
cohort: The study included 23 patients with postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony who received Alcides-Pereira's sutures at a single tertiary hospital over an 11-year period.
finding: Alcides-Pereira's sutures were successful in controlling hemorrhage and avoiding hysterectomy in 87% of patients with PPH due to uterine atony, also significantly reducing the need for blood therapy, ICU admission, and hospital stay.
mod_finding: One patient with preserved uterus had a subsequent term vaginal delivery.
